metadata.title: Exact Recovery in the Stochastic Block Model

nodes.name: Stochastic Block Model $\mathcal{G}(n,p,q)$ (planted bisection)
nodes.statement: For even $n$, each vertex $v \in [n]$ is assigned a uniform binary label $X_v$ with $|\{v : X_v=1\}|=n/2$; conditionally on labels, edges are independent with probability $p$ if $X_u=X_v$ and $q$ if $X_u \neq X_v$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random graph with two equally sized communities, intra-cluster edge probability p, inter-cluster edge probability q.

nodes.name: Exact recovery
nodes.statement: Recovery of the true partition with probability tending to one as $n \to \infty$ (up to a global flip of labels).
nodes.statement_clean: Recover the bipartition with probability going to 1.

nodes.name: Failure events $F, F_A, \Delta, F_H^{(j)}, F_H$
nodes.statement: $F$=ML fails; $F_A$=$\exists i \in A$ connected to more nodes in $B$ than in $A$; $\Delta$=no node in $H$ has degree $\geq \delta(n)$ in $H$; $F_H^{(j)}=\{E(j,A\setminus H)+\delta(n)\leq E(j,B)\}$; $F_H=\cup_{j\in H}F_H^{(j)}$, where $H \subset A$ has size $n/\gamma(n)$, $\gamma(n)=\log^3 n$, $\delta(n)=\log n / \log\log n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Auxiliary failure events used to bound the probability that ML fails.

nodes.name: Tail function $T(N,p,q,\eps)$
nodes.statement: $T(N,p,q,\eps)=\mathbb{P}\!\left( \sum_{i=1}^N (Z_i - W_i) \geq \eps \right)$ with $W_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$ i.i.d., $Z_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(q)$ i.i.d., independent.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail probability of the difference of two independent binomials.

nodes.name: Stochastic Block Model Laplacian $L_{SBM}$
nodes.statement: $L_{SBM} = D_{\mathcal{G}}^+ - D_{\mathcal{G}}^- - A$, where $D_{\mathcal{G}}^+$ (resp. $D_{\mathcal{G}}^-$) is the degree matrix of the within-community (resp. across-community) subgraph and $A$ is the adjacency matrix of $\mathcal{G}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Signed graph Laplacian using within- minus across-community degrees minus adjacency.

nodes.name: Dominant term $T^*(m,p,q,\epsilon)$
nodes.statement: $T^*(m,p,q,\epsilon)=\max_{\tau>0} V(m,p,q,\tau,\epsilon)$, where $V(m,p,q,\tau,\epsilon)$ is a single-term binomial product (see Lemma~1) used to upper-bound $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Dominant binomial term used to estimate the tail T.

nodes.name: Maximum likelihood / min-bisection problem
nodes.section: 3 Information theoretic perspective and main results
nodes.statement: Find a balanced partition of $V$ into $(A_{ML},B_{ML})$ with $|A_{ML}|=|B_{ML}|=n/2$ minimising the number of edges across the cut: $\arg\min_{|A|=|B|=n/2} E(A,B)$ (when $\alpha>\beta$). NP-hard in the worst case.
nodes.statement_clean: Find a balanced bipartition minimizing the cut size; equivalent to ML when communities are uniform.

nodes.name: Combinatorial $\pm 1$ formulation
nodes.statement: $\max_{x \in \{\pm 1\}^n} x^T B x$, where $B_{ij}=1$ if $(i,j)\in E(\mathcal{G})$, $B_{ij}=-1$ if $(i,j) \notin E(\mathcal{G})$, $B_{ii}=0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Quadratic combinatorial maximization over sign vectors used as ML reformulation.

nodes.name: SDP relaxation of ML
nodes.statement: $\max_{X \succeq 0, X_{ii}=1} \mathrm{Tr}(BX)$ -- the Goemans-Williamson-style semidefinite relaxation of $\max_{x\in\{\pm 1\}^n} x^T B x$.
nodes.statement_clean: SDP relaxation of the combinatorial cut maximization.

nodes.name: Recovery threshold formula
nodes.statement: $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} > 1$, equivalently $\alpha+\beta>2$ and $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 4(\alpha+\beta)-4$, equivalently $\sqrt{\alpha}-\sqrt{\beta}>1$ for $\alpha>\beta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp threshold expression separating recoverable from unrecoverable regimes.

nodes.name: Dual feasibility / PSD condition for SDP
nodes.statement: $2L_{SBM}+I_n - \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T \succeq 0$ and $\lambda_2(2L_{SBM}+I_n-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T) > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: PSD-and-second-eigenvalue condition implying $gg^T$ is the unique SDP optimum.

nodes.name: Information-theoretic lower bound (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha>\beta\geq 0$. If $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} < 1$ (equivalently $\alpha+\beta<2$, or $\alpha+\beta\geq 2$ and $(\alpha-\beta)^2 < 4(\alpha+\beta)-4$), then ML fails to recover the communities with probability bounded away from zero.
nodes.statement_clean: Below the threshold, ML cannot exactly recover the communities w.h.p.

nodes.name: Information-theoretic upper bound (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: If $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} > 1$ (i.e. $\alpha+\beta>2$ and $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 4(\alpha+\beta)-4$), then ML exactly recovers the communities (up to a global flip) with high probability.
nodes.statement_clean: Above the threshold, ML achieves exact recovery w.h.p.

nodes.name: SDP recovery guarantee (Theorem 3)
nodes.statement: If $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 8(\alpha+\beta) + \frac{8}{3}(\alpha-\beta)$, then with high probability the SDP $\max_{X \succeq 0, X_{ii}=1} \mathrm{Tr}(BX)$ has unique optimum $gg^T$, where $g_i=\pm 1$ encodes the communities; hence exact recovery is possible in polynomial time.
nodes.statement_clean: Under a slightly looser threshold, the SDP relaxation exactly recovers the communities in polynomial time.

nodes.name: Efficient algorithm achieving the threshold (Theorem 4)
nodes.section: 6.2 Efficient full recovery from efficient partial recovery
nodes.statement: If $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} > 1$, then there exists $C=C(\alpha,\beta)$ large enough such that the partition-then-local-flip algorithm succeeds with high probability in recovering the communities from $\mathcal{G}(n,p,q)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An efficient algorithm matching the IT threshold exists, via partial recovery + local improvements.
conclusions: polynomial-time algorithm exactly recovers the communities w.h.p.

nodes.name: Matrix Bernstein inequality
nodes.statement: For independent self-adjoint $d\times d$ matrices $\{X_k\}$ with $\mathbb{E}X_k=0$ and $\lambda_{\max}(X_k)\leq R$ a.s., $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\lambda_{\max}(\sum_k X_k) \geq t\right) \leq d\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2/2}{\sigma^2 + Rt/3}\right)$, where $\sigma^2 = \| \sum_k \mathbb{E} X_k^2 \|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Concentration tail bound for sums of independent self-adjoint matrices.
nodes.origin_citation: Tropp, User-Friendly Tail Bounds for Sums of Random Matrices (2012)

nodes.name: Detection threshold for SBM (cited)
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{G}(n,a/n,b/n)$, detection (recovering more than $(1/2+\eps)n$ vertices correctly) is possible if and only if $(a-b)^2 > 2(a+b)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp detection threshold for sparse SBM, used as reference for the recovery problem.

nodes.name: ER connectivity threshold (cited)
nodes.statement: For Erdos-Renyi $G(n,p)$ with $p = c\log n / n$, the graph is connected w.h.p. if $c>1$ and disconnected w.h.p. if $c<1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical sharp connectivity threshold for ER; necessary condition for SBM recovery.

nodes.name: Lemma (failure on $A$ implies ML failure)
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{P}(F_A) \geq 2/3$ then $\mathbb{P}(F) \geq 1/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: If a failure event in side A holds w.p. at least 2/3, ML fails with prob at least 1/3.

nodes.name: Lemma (reverse union bound on $F_H$)
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{P}(F_H) \geq 9/10$ then $\mathbb{P}(F) \geq 1/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lower bound on ML failure via the H-event probability.

nodes.name: Lemma (controlling $\rho(n)$ suffices)
nodes.statement: Let $\rho(n)=\mathbb{P}(F_H^{(i)})$. If $\rho(n) > n^{-1}\gamma(n)\log(10)$ then for sufficiently large $n$, $\mathbb{P}(F) \geq 1/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: A lower bound on the per-node failure probability rho(n) suffices for ML failure.

nodes.name: Lemma (asymptotic of $-\log T$)
nodes.statement: For $\alpha>\beta>0$, $-\log T\!\left(n/2, \alpha\log n/n, \beta\log n/n, \log n/\log\log n\right) \leq \left( (\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} \right)\log n + o(\log n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp bound on the log-tail of difference of binomials in the SBM regime.

nodes.name: Lemma (ML failure $\Rightarrow$ disagreement set witness)
nodes.statement: If ML does not coincide with the ground truth, then there exist $1\leq k\leq n/4$, $A_w \subset A$, $B_w \subset B$ with $|A_w|=|B_w|=k$ such that $E(A_w,B\setminus B_w) + E(B_w,A\setminus A_w) \geq E(A_w,A\setminus A_w) + E(B_w,B\setminus B_w)$.
nodes.statement_clean: ML failure is witnessed by a balanced swap of equal-size subsets.

nodes.name: Lemma $P_n^{(k)}$ Bernstein bound
nodes.statement: $T\!\left(m, \alpha\log n/n, \beta\log n/n, 0\right) \leq \exp\!\left( -\frac{2m}{n} \left( \frac{\alpha+\beta}{2} - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} + o(1) \right) \log n \right)$ for $n$ large, where $m=2k(n/2-k)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Exponential bound on the binomial-difference tail used in the union bound for ML success.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (binomial dominant-term bounds)
nodes.statement: Define $g(\alpha,\beta,\epsilon)=(\alpha+\beta) - \epsilon\log(\beta) - 2\sqrt{(\epsilon/2)^2 + \alpha\beta} + (\epsilon/2)\log\!\left( \alpha\beta \frac{\sqrt{(\epsilon/2)^2+\alpha\beta}+\epsilon/2}{\sqrt{(\epsilon/2)^2+\alpha\beta}-\epsilon/2} \right)$. Then $-\log T^*(m,p,q,\epsilon) \geq (m/n)\log(n)\,g(\alpha,\beta,\epsilon) - o((m/n)\log n)$, and for $cn \leq m < c'n^{3/2}$, $-\log T^*(m,p,q,\epsilon) \leq (m/n)\log(n)\,g(\alpha,\beta,\epsilon) + o((m/n)\log n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two-sided bounds on the dominant binomial term via the function g(alpha,beta,epsilon).

nodes.name: Lemma (mislabel-probability upper bound)
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}\!\left( \sum_{i=1}^{(1-\delta)n/2} Z_i + \sum_{i=1}^{\delta n/2} W_i \geq \sum_{i=1}^{(1-\delta)n/2 - 2Cn/\log n} W'_i + \sum_{i=1}^{\delta n/2 - 2Cn/\log n} Z'_i \right) \leq n^{-(g(\alpha,\beta,-\gamma\delta(C))+o(1))} + n^{-(1+\Omega(1))}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bound on the probability that a node is mislabeled in the partial-recovery + local-flip algorithm.

nodes.name: Lemma ($\mathbb{P}(\Delta) \geq 9/10$)
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{P}(\Delta) \geq 9/10$, where $\Delta$ is the event that in a graph on $n/\log^3 n$ vertices with edge probability $\alpha\log n/n$, every node has degree $< \log n / \log\log n$.
nodes.statement_clean: With probability at least 9/10, no node in the small subgraph H has many H-neighbours.

nodes.name: Lemma (KKT/dual sufficient condition for SDP)
nodes.statement: If $2L_{SBM}+I_n-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T \succeq 0$ and $\lambda_2(2L_{SBM}+I_n-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T) > 0$, then $gg^T$ is the unique optimum of the SDP $\max_{X\succeq 0, X_{ii}=1}\mathrm{Tr}(BX)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sufficient PSD/eigenvalue conditions for the SDP to recover the planted partition uniquely.

nodes.name: Lemma (reduction to spectral norm of $\Gamma$ projections)
nodes.statement: If $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}) \geq n - 2\beta\log n) < n^{-\epsilon}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}) \geq (\alpha-\beta)\log n) < n^{-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, then condition $C-\Gamma \succeq 0$ and $\lambda_{\min}(C^{\perp g}-\Gamma^{\perp g})>0$ holds w.h.p.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduces SDP success conditions to two spectral-norm tail bounds on Gamma.

nodes.name: Lemma ($\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}$ tail bound)
nodes.statement: For $n$ large, $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}) \geq n - 2\beta\log n\right) < n^{-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail bound for the projection of Gamma onto span(1) via Matrix Bernstein.

nodes.name: Lemma ($\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}$ tail bound)
nodes.statement: If $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 8(\alpha+\beta) + \frac{8}{3}(\alpha-\beta)$, then $\mathbb{P}\!\left(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}) \geq (\alpha-\beta)\log n\right) < n^{-\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail bound for the orthogonal-to-1 projection of Gamma; key step for SDP recovery.

nodes.name: Lemma (degree of $H_1$ nodes)
nodes.statement: With high probability, every node in $H_1$ has degree at most $2Cn/\log n$, where $H_1$ is an Erdos-Renyi graph on $n$ nodes with edge probability $C/\log n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Uniform bound on degrees in the auxiliary graph H_1 used to split edges.

nodes.name: SDP-based community recovery
nodes.statement: Solve the SDP $\max_{X\succeq 0, X_{ii}=1} \mathrm{Tr}(BX)$ on the $\pm 1$-signed adjacency-like matrix $B$, recover communities from the rank-1 optimum $gg^T$.
input: Signed matrix $B$ with $B_{ij}=1$ if $(i,j)\in E(\mathcal{G})$, $B_{ij}=-1$ else, $B_{ii}=0$
output: Community assignment vector $g \in \{\pm 1\}^n$ (up to global flip)

nodes.name: Partial recovery + local improvement (two-step)
nodes.section: 6.2 Efficient full recovery from efficient partial recovery
nodes.statement: Split edges into $G_1=H_1\cap\mathcal{G}$ (sparse) and $G_2=H_2\cap\mathcal{G}$; run partial-recovery (Massoulie) on $G_1$ to obtain $(A',B')$; flip each node whose $G_2$-neighbour majority points to the opposite cluster; revert if flip counts are unbalanced.
output: Refined partition $(A^*,B^*)$ achieving exact recovery w.h.p. when $(\alpha+\beta)/2-\sqrt{\alpha\beta}>1$

nodes.name: Massoulie's partial-recovery algorithm
nodes.statement: Spectral / non-backtracking algorithm that, for the sparse SBM with parameters $(C\alpha, C\beta)$, produces a partition $(A',B')$ correct on at least $(1-\delta(C))n$ nodes w.h.p., with $\delta(C)\to 0$ as $C\to\infty$.
output: Partition $(A',B')$ correlated with the truth on $\geq (1-\delta(C))n$ nodes
nodes.origin_citation: Massoulie 2014 (Community detection thresholds and the weak Ramanujan property)

nodes.name: Maximum likelihood (min-bisection) decoder
nodes.statement: Among balanced bipartitions, return one with the fewest cross-edges (equivalently, maximum likelihood when communities are uniform). Information-theoretically optimal but NP-hard in the worst case.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (lower bound)
nodes.statement: Show $\rho(n) > n^{-1}\gamma(n)\log(10)$ via the asymptotic of $-\log T$ (Lemma~LP3.4); then by Lemma LP3.3 we get $\mathbb{P}(F)\geq 1/3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (upper bound)
nodes.statement: Union-bound over swapped subsets of size $k\in[1,n/4]$, apply the binomial-difference Bernstein bound (Lemma~LP3.6), and use ${n\choose k}\leq (ne/k)^k$ to obtain $\mathbb{P}(F)\leq cn^{-\epsilon/4}$ when $(\alpha+\beta)/2-\sqrt{\alpha\beta}>1+\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 (SDP guarantee)
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP3.10, the dual-feasibility/PSD condition implies SDP optimality of $gg^T$. Decompose $2L_{SBM}+I_n-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T = C-\Gamma$, reduce (Lemma LP3.11) to two tail bounds on $\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}$ and $\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}$ (Lemmas LP3.12-13), proven via Matrix Bernstein under $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 8(\alpha+\beta) + 8(\alpha-\beta)/3$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4 (efficient threshold-achieving algorithm)
nodes.statement: Use the random edge split (Lemma LP3.14) to make partial recovery on $G_1$ near-independent of local-flip step on $G_2$; bound mislabel probability per node via Lemma LP3.8; union-bound over $n$ nodes; choose $C$ large so $\delta(C)\to 0$ and $1-((\alpha+\beta)/2-\sqrt{\alpha\beta}) < 0$.

nodes.name: Setup events and $\rho(n)$
nodes.statement: Recall the failure events $F, F_A, \Delta, F_H^{(j)}, F_H$ from (\ref{def:events}) and define $\rho(n) = \mathbb{P}(F_H^{(i)})$ as the per-node failure probability over $H \subset A$ of size $n/\gamma(n)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma LP3.4 to bound $-\log\rho(n)$
nodes.statement: Since $\rho(n) \geq T(n/2,p,q,\log n/\log\log n)$ (after dropping the $H$-correction in the sum), Lemma LP3.4 gives $-\log \rho(n) \leq ((\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta})\log n + o(\log n)$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\rho(n) > n^{-1}\gamma(n)\log(10)$
nodes.statement: Under the assumption $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} < 1$, the previous bound implies $\rho(n) \geq n^{-((\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta} + o(1))} > n^{-1}\gamma(n)\log(10)$ for large $n$.

nodes.name: Conclude via Lemma LP3.3 that $\mathbb{P}(F)\geq 1/3$
nodes.statement: Plugging the lower bound on $\rho(n)$ into Lemma LP3.3 yields $\mathbb{P}(F) \geq 1/3$, i.e. ML fails with probability bounded away from zero.

nodes.name: Witness lemma for ML failure
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP3.5, ML failure implies the existence of equally sized swap sets $A_w \subset A$, $B_w \subset B$ with $|A_w|=|B_w|=k\leq n/4$ such that the cross-edge counts dominate the within-cluster edge counts.

nodes.name: Identify witness probability with $T$
nodes.statement: For fixed $A_w, B_w$ of size $k$, $P_n^{(k)} := \mathbb{P}(\text{witness condition}) = T(2k(n/2-k), \alpha\log n/n, \beta\log n/n, 0)$.

nodes.name: Union bound over witness sets
nodes.statement: By a union bound over choices of $A_w$ and $B_w$, $\mathbb{P}(F) \leq \sum_{k=1}^{n/4} {n/2 \choose k}^2 P_n^{(k)}$.

nodes.name: Apply binomial-difference Bernstein bound (Lemma LP3.6)
nodes.statement: Lemma LP3.6 gives $P_n^{(k)} \leq \exp(-(\log n/n) \cdot 4k(n/2-k)((\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta}))$.

nodes.name: Substitute ${n\choose k} \leq (ne/k)^k$
nodes.statement: Using ${n/2 \choose k} \leq (ne/(2k))^k$ and the previous bound, simplify the summand to $\exp[k(2\log n - 2\log 2k + 2 - (1/2-k/n)\cdot 4((\alpha+\beta)/2-\sqrt{\alpha\beta})\log n)]$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\mathbb{P}(F) \leq c n^{-\epsilon/4}$
nodes.statement: Assuming $(\alpha+\beta)/2 -\sqrt{\alpha\beta} \geq 1+\epsilon$, factor $n^{-\epsilon/4}$ out of each summand and bound $\sum_k \exp[-\frac23 k(\log 2k - 3)] = O(1)$ to obtain $\mathbb{P}(F) \leq c n^{-\epsilon/4} \to 0$.

nodes.name: KKT setup: dual certificate $Y = 2(D^+-D^-)+I_n$
nodes.statement: Apply KKT to the SDP (\ref{SDP:mainSDP}); $gg^T$ is primal-feasible. To obtain strong duality, build the diagonal dual matrix $Y = 2(D_{\mathcal{G}}^+ - D_{\mathcal{G}}^-) + I_n$ satisfying $\mathrm{Tr}(Bgg^T) = \mathrm{Tr}(Y)$.

nodes.name: Optimality and uniqueness via Lemma LP3.10
nodes.statement: Dual feasibility $Y \succeq B$ becomes $2L_{SBM}+I_n - \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T \succeq 0$; the second-eigenvalue condition $\lambda_2 > 0$ then forces $X^* = gg^T$ uniquely (Lemma LP3.10).

nodes.name: Decompose $2L_{SBM}+I_n - \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T = C - \Gamma$
nodes.statement: Rewrite the SDP matrix as a deterministic mean $C$ minus a zero-mean random matrix $\Gamma$ using elementary matrices $\Delta_{ij}^\pm$ and Bernoulli signs $\alpha_{ij}^\pm$.

nodes.name: Reduce to spectral tail bounds (Lemma LP3.11)
nodes.statement: Lemma LP3.11 shows it suffices to prove $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}) \geq n - 2\beta\log n) < n^{-\epsilon}$ and $\mathbb{P}(\lambda_{\max}(\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}) \geq (\alpha-\beta)\log n) < n^{-\epsilon}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}$ tail via Matrix Bernstein (Lemma LP3.12)
nodes.statement: Apply Matrix Bernstein with $R = O(1/n)$ and $\sigma^2 = O(\beta\log n/n)$ to bound the projection $\Gamma^{\mathbf{1}}$, giving Lemma LP3.12 unconditionally for large $n$.

nodes.name: Bound $\Gamma^{\perp\mathbf{1}}$ tail via Matrix Bernstein (Lemma LP3.13)
nodes.statement: Apply Matrix Bernstein with $R=4$ and $\sigma^2 = 4(\alpha+\beta)\log n + O(\log^2 n /n)$; the resulting tail is $< n^{-\epsilon}$ exactly when $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 8(\alpha+\beta) + 8(\alpha-\beta)/3$.

nodes.name: Conclude SDP recovery
nodes.statement: Combining steps PSP3.12, PSP3.14-PSP3.16, the dual-feasibility condition holds w.h.p., so $gg^T$ is the unique SDP optimum and exact recovery is achieved in polynomial time.

nodes.name: Setup: assume partial recovery succeeds on $G_1$
nodes.statement: Assume Massoulie's algorithm on the sparse split $G_1$ outputs $(A',B')$ correct on $\geq (1-\delta(C))n$ nodes w.h.p.; aim to bound the probability that any node remains mislabeled after the local-flip step on $G_2$.

nodes.name: Reduce $H_2$ to almost-complete via Lemma LP3.14
nodes.statement: Using Lemma LP3.14, the degree of every node in $H_2$ is at least $n(1 - 2C/\log n)$ w.h.p., so we may upper-bound the mislabel probability by removing $2Cn/\log n$ from the right-hand-side sums.

nodes.name: Express mislabel probability $P_e$ as Bernoulli-difference tail
nodes.statement: For a node $e$, $P_e = \mathbb{P}\!\left( \sum_{i=1}^{(1-\delta(C))n/2} Z_i + \sum_{i=1}^{\delta(C)n/2} W_i \geq \sum_{i=1}^{(1-\delta(C))n/2} W'_i + \sum_{i=1}^{\delta(C)n/2} Z'_i \right)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma LP3.8 to bound $P_e$
nodes.statement: Lemma LP3.8 gives $P_e \leq n^{-(g(\alpha,\beta,-\gamma\delta(C))+o(1))} + n^{-(1+\Omega(1))}$, where $\gamma = 1/(\delta(C)\sqrt{\log(1/\delta(C))})$ and $g(\alpha,\beta,\delta') \to (\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta}$ as $\delta'\to 0$.

nodes.name: Union bound over nodes and conclude
nodes.statement: Union-bound: $\mathbb{P}(\exists\text{ mislabeled node}) \leq n \cdot P_e \leq n^{1 - g(\alpha,\beta,-\gamma\delta(C)) - o(1)} + n^{-\Omega(1)} \to 0$ for $C$ large enough so that $\delta(C)$ is small and $1 - g(\alpha,\beta,0) = 1 - ((\alpha+\beta)/2-\sqrt{\alpha\beta}) < 0$.

nodes.name: Random edge split
nodes.statement: Independently of $\mathcal{G}$, partition the edges of the complete graph $K_n$ into $H_1$ (Erdos-Renyi with edge probability $C/\log n$) and $H_2 = K_n \setminus H_1$.

nodes.name: Form subgraphs $G_1, G_2$
nodes.statement: Set $G_1 = H_1 \cap \mathcal{G}$ (a sparse SBM with parameters $(C\alpha, C\beta)$) and $G_2 = H_2 \cap \mathcal{G}$ (the remaining edges).

nodes.name: Run Massoulie partial recovery on $G_1$
nodes.statement: Apply Massoulie's algorithm (AP3.3) to $G_1$ to obtain a partition $(A', B')$ correct on at least $(1-\delta(C))n$ nodes w.h.p.

nodes.name: Local flip in $G_2$ (loop over nodes)
nodes.statement: For each node $v$: count its $G_2$-edges to its currently assigned cluster vs.\ to the opposite cluster; if more $G_2$-edges go to the opposite cluster, flip $v$'s label.

nodes.name: Balance check / revert
nodes.statement: If the number of flips in the two clusters differ, revert all flips and keep $(A', B')$ unchanged; otherwise output the flipped partition $(A^*, B^*)$.

nodes.name: Return the refined partition
nodes.statement: Output the (possibly flipped) partition as the recovered communities.

nodes.name: Construct signed matrix $B$
nodes.statement: Form $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with $B_{ii}=0$, $B_{ij}=1$ if $(i,j)\in E(\mathcal{G})$, $B_{ij}=-1$ otherwise.

nodes.name: Solve SDP $\max \mathrm{Tr}(BX)$
nodes.statement: Solve $\max_{X \succeq 0,\, X_{ii}=1} \mathrm{Tr}(BX)$ to obtain optimum $X^*$ via interior-point or other polynomial-time SDP solver.

nodes.name: Extract communities from rank-1 optimum
nodes.statement: When the SDP optimum is rank-1 (the case under Theorem 3), $X^* = gg^T$ for some $g \in \{\pm 1\}^n$ encoding the two communities; output $g$.

nodes.name: Direct SDP/spectral algorithm achieving the IT threshold
nodes.statement: Show that the SDP relaxation (or a spectral algorithm) achieves exact recovery all the way down to the optimal threshold $(\alpha+\beta)/2 - \sqrt{\alpha\beta}>1$, removing the factor-2 looseness from the Matrix Bernstein analysis.
nodes.statement_clean: Open: prove the SDP (or spectral) algorithm matches the IT recovery threshold directly.

nodes.name: Relation between detection and recovery thresholds
nodes.statement: Determine whether efficient algorithms achieving the detection threshold $(a-b)^2 > 2(a+b)$ can also achieve the recovery threshold (and vice versa), or whether the two thresholds require fundamentally different algorithmic approaches.
nodes.statement_clean: Open: are detection-optimal and recovery-optimal algorithms related?

nodes.name: Generalisation to more complex SBM models
nodes.statement: Extend the sharp threshold result to more general network models with multiple communities, overlapping (mixed-membership) communities, or labelled edges.
nodes.statement_clean: Open: extend the sharp threshold to multi-community, overlapping, or labelled SBMs.

nodes.name: Numerical evidence: SDP matches IT threshold
nodes.statement: Numerical simulations ($n=300$, 20 trials) suggest the SDP-based algorithm achieves exact recovery essentially down to the optimal threshold $(\alpha-\beta)^2 = 4(\alpha+\beta)-4$, despite the analysis only proving recovery for the looser threshold $(\alpha-\beta)^2 > 8(\alpha+\beta)+8(\alpha-\beta)/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirically, the SDP appears to attain the IT threshold; the factor-2 gap is likely a Matrix-Bernstein analysis artifact.

nodes.name: Standard CLT/Chernoff/Sanov insufficient
nodes.statement: Standard estimates (CLT, Chernoff, Sanov) do not yield the sharp $(\alpha+\beta)/2 -\sqrt{\alpha\beta}$ exponent, because their error on the exponent is $O(\log n)$ -- of the same order as the leading term -- owing to the slow concentration in the regime $p,q = \Theta(\log n / n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp threshold cannot be obtained by classical concentration; tighter binomial estimates are required.

nodes.name: Numerical SDP success-probability experiment
nodes.statement: For $n=300$ and 20 trials per parameter pair, compute the empirical success probability of SDP recovery; observe the empirical threshold matches the IT threshold curve $(\alpha-\beta)^2 = 4(\alpha+\beta)-4$ rather than the proven SDP curve $(\alpha-\beta)^2 = 8(\alpha+\beta) + 8(\alpha-\beta)/3$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical experiment plotting SDP success rate against alpha,beta.
